items.stem: A FIXED level-of-detail expression computes a value at which granularity?

options.text: The dimensions named in the expression, regardless of the view's level of detail
options.rationale: Correct: FIXED pins the computation to the stated dimensions, ignoring the view.

options.text: Always the most granular row in the data source
options.rationale: FIXED uses the stated dimensions, not necessarily row level.

options.text: Whatever dimensions are on the Rows shelf only
options.rationale: That describes the view's detail, which FIXED overrides.
FIXED is computed before dimension filters, not from the selection alone.

items.explanation: Correct: FIXED pins the computation to the stated dimensions, ignoring the view.

items.stem: Which TWO are true about joins versus data blending in Tableau? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A join combines tables at the row level before aggregation
options.rationale: Correct: joins merge rows prior to aggregation.

options.text: Blending aggregates each source separately and combines the results on a linking field
options.rationale: Correct: blending joins aggregated results on a common field.

options.text: Blending always produces the same granularity as an inner join
options.rationale: Blending works on aggregates, so granularity differs from a row-level join.

options.text: Joins can only be used across different database servers
options.rationale: Joins are typically within one source; cross-source needs relationships or blending.

items.explanation: Correct: joins merge rows prior to aggregation.

items.stem: You want clicking a bar in one chart to filter a second chart on the same dashboard. What do you use?

options.text: A filter action configured on the dashboard
options.rationale: Correct: a filter action passes the selection as a filter to the target.

options.text: A calculated field on each worksheet
options.rationale: Calculated fields do not create cross-chart interaction.

options.text: A separate data source for each chart
options.rationale: That does not create the interaction either.

options.text: Changing the mark type to a map
options.rationale: Mark type is unrelated to cross-chart filtering.

items.explanation: Correct: a filter action passes the selection as a filter to the target.
